cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where user-supplied data flows into sensitive operations (file I/O, shell execution, SQL queries, database updates, configuration modifications) without proper validation, sanitization, or authorization checks. The issues include path traversal, command injection, SQL injection, mass assignment, and missing authorization for security-critical configuration options.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets into sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource. Report code paths where the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation.

mechanism.missing_guard: the authorization decision is not bound to both the current principal and the exact resource or tenant being affected
mechanism.name: missing object-owner or tenant-scope authorization
mechanism.sink_shape: sensitive read, write, mutation, deletion, workflow, or administrative operations on the selected resource
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-selected resource identifiers, object IDs, tenant IDs, or administrative action targets
mechanism.typical_fix: check ownership or tenant scope before the effect and carry that checked identity into the data access or mutation

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add the vulnerable options to an admin-only set and enforce role checks before allowing modification.
sub_patterns.name: Missing authorization for sensitive configuration options
sub_patterns.root_cause: Certain configuration options that affect security (e.g., plugin exec path, storage folder) are not restricted to admin users, allowing low-privileged users to modify them.
